item.title: Prepare by Reviewing Grades 1–2 Curriculum... Low Scores Are Okay (1~2학년 과정 복습 위주로 대비…성적 낮아도 괜찮아요)
item.description:
The National United Achievement Test (hereafter referred to as the academic assessment), the first CSAT mock exam for high school seniors taking the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), will be held on March 24. This test is administered by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, not by the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation (KICE), which oversees the CSAT. Graduates do not take it, and its scope of questions differs from the actual CSAT scheduled for November 19, so there are limits to using it for college admissions. (2027학년도 대학수학능력시험을 치르는 고교 3학년의 첫 수능 모의고사인 전국연합학력평가(이하 학평)가 3월24일에 치러진다. 이번 시험은 수능 출제기관인 한국교육과정평가원이 아닌 서울교육청이 주관하고, 졸업생이 응시하지 않으며, 11월19일 치러지는 실제 수능과 출제범위 등이 달라 입시에 활용하기에는 한계가 있다.)

However, the March academic assessment is a prime opportunity to objectively evaluate your skills so far and identify your current standing, weak areas, and units. Since it's the first mock exam after becoming a senior, the pressure may be considerable, but you should keep in mind that it's a "practice test" and use it as a chance to gain real exam experience. Based on data from Jinhaksa Admissions Strategy Research Institute, Visang Education Admissions Evaluation Institute, 1318 University Admissions Research Institute, Etus Education Evaluation Research Institute, and Uway Education Evaluation Research Institute, we've compiled preparation and utilization strategies for the March academic assessment. (하지만 3월 학평은 지금까지 본인의 실력을 객관적으로 평가해 현재 자신의 위치와 취약영역과 단원 등을 파악할 수 있는 절호의 기회다. 고3이 되고나서 치르는 첫 모의고사라는 점에서 부담이 적지 않겠지만, ‘연습시험’이라는 점을 염두에 두고 실전 경험을 쌓는 기회로 삼아야 한다. 진학사 입시전략연구소, 비상교육 입시평가소, 1318대학진학연구소, 이투스 교육평가연구소, 유웨이 교육평가연구소의 자료를 바탕으로 3월 학평 대비 및 활용법을 정리했다.)

Prepare by Focusing on Review and Concept Organization (복습과 개념 정리 위주로 대비)

The March academic assessment is a test that gauges how much you've studied so far. Its main purpose is to provide individual scores and grades. Therefore, rather than studying simply to do well on the March assessment, you should prepare with the mindset of assessing your current level of ability. (3월 학평은 지금까지 본인이 얼마나 공부를 해왔는지를 가늠하는 시험이다. 개인별 성적과 등급 등을 제공하는 데 주된 목적이 있다. 이 때문에 단순히 3월 학평을 잘 보기 위해 공부를 하기보다는 현재 내 실력이 어느 정도인지 판단해보자는 마음으로 준비해야 한다.)

The scope of the March academic assessment covers the entire grades 1–2 curriculum for Korean and English, the full common subject scope of Mathematics I and Mathematics II for math, and for elective subjects: Probability and Statistics covers "I. Number of Cases," Calculus covers "I. Limits of Sequences," and Geometry covers "I. Conic Sections." In other words, since questions come only from what was learned in grades 1 and 2, it's advantageous to prepare before the test by reviewing areas or weak units from up to 2nd grade. After this period, there won't be many chances to review, so it's better to treat this opportunity as a period dedicated to final review. (3월 학평은 출제 범위가 국어와 영어 영역의 경우 고등학교 1, 2학년 전 범위, 수학 영역은 공통 과목인 수학Ⅰ, 수학Ⅱ 전 범위이고, 선택 과목인 확률과통계는 ‘Ⅰ. 경우의 수’, 미적분은 ‘Ⅰ. 수열의 극한’, 기하는 ‘Ⅰ. 이차곡선’ 등이다. 즉 1, 2학년 때 배운 내용에서만 출제되는 점을 감안, 시험 전에는 2학년 때까지 본인이 부족한 영역이나 취약 단원 위주로 복습을 하며 준비하는 것이 유리하다. 이 시기를 지나면 복습할 수 있는 기회가 많지 않기 때문에 이번 기회를 마지막 복습에 매진하는 기간으로 삼는 것이 낫다는 것이다.)

Yoo Seong-ryong, director of the 1318 University Admissions Research Institute, said, "If your grades by subject on academic assessments taken up to 2nd grade were within grades 1–2, it's fine to do advanced preparation using past CSAT questions or EBS CSAT Essentials." He added, "But if you were at grade 3 or below, rather than advanced CSAT preparation, it's most important to review the grades 1–2 curriculum again by subject." In this regard, Director Yoo recommended that students be sure to review textbooks or reference books they've used so far. (유성룡 1318대학진학연구소장은 “2학년 때까지 치른 학력평가의 영역별 등급이 1, 2등급 이내였다면, 그동안 출제된 수능시험 기출 문제나 EBS 수능특강 등을 통해 선행적인 대비를 해도 괜찮다”며 “하지만 3등급 이하였다면 선행적인 수능시험 대비보다는 교과목별로 고교 1, 2학년 과정을 다시 복습하는 것이 무엇보다 중요하다”고 말했다. 이와 관련해 유 소장은 지금껏 봐온 교과서나 참고서 등을 꼭 다시 한번 복습하길 권했다.)

Additionally, Director Yoo Seong-ryong said, "Study time by subject for students at grade 3 or below may vary depending on each student's individual achievement in each subject," but suggested, "However, for students applying to mid-to-upper-tier humanities programs, allocate study time in the order of Korean > Math > Social Studies > English, and for students applying to science programs, in the order of Math > Science > Korean > English." (또한, 유성룡 소장은 “3등급 이하 학생들의 교과목별 공부 시간은 학생 개개인의 과목별 성취도에 따라 차이가 있을 수 있다”면서도 “하지만 중상위권 인문계 모집단위 지원 학생은 국어 > 수학 > 사회탐구 > 영어 순으로, 자연계 모집단위 지원 학생은 수학 > 과학탐구 > 국어 > 영어 순으로 비중을 두고, 그에 따른 학습 시간을 배정하고 공부했으면 한다”고 제안했다.)

Woo Yeon-cheol, director of Jinhaksa Admissions Strategy Research Institute, advised, "With the March academic assessment just around the corner, some students rush to solve as many problems as possible in a hurry. But compared to such problem-solving, the learning process of organizing insufficient concepts is more important." He added, "Using existing materials, it's necessary to identify concepts you don't know well or concepts you repeatedly get wrong, focusing on wrong answers, and thoroughly organize them." (우연철 진학사 입시전략연구소장은 “3월 학평이 얼마 남지 않은 시점에서 급한 마음에 무작정 많은 문제를 풀려는 학생들이 있다. 하지만 이런 문제 풀이보다는 부족한 개념을 정리해가는 학습 과정이 더 중요하다”며 “기존 교재를 가지고 틀린 문제를 중심으로 자신이 잘 모르는 개념, 반복적으로 틀리는 개념 등을 확인하고 확실히 정리하는 것이 필요하다”고 조언했다.)

Once concept organization is somewhat complete, solving past exam questions from the last three years is recommended. For high school seniors just beginning the full-fledged college admissions race, school exam-style problems will likely still feel more familiar than CSAT-style ones. Therefore, if you haven't experienced CSAT-style questions in advance, you might be flustered the moment you receive the test paper. So it's necessary to use past CSAT, academic assessment, and mock evaluation questions within the scope of the last three years to see how concepts are applied in problems and train yourself to become familiar with new question types. (개념정리가 어느 정도 됐다면 최근 3년간의 기출문제를 푸는 것을 추천한다. 이제 막 본격적인 대입 레이스에 참가하는 고3 학생들에게는 아직까지 수능형 문제보다는 내신형 문제가 더 익숙할 것이다. 그렇기에 수능형 문제를 미리 경험해보지 않으면 시험지를 받아 보는 순간 당황할 수 있다. 따라서 최근 3년간의 출제범위 내 수능, 학력평가, 모의평가의 기출문제를 통해 개념이 문제에서 어떻게 활용되는지 파악하고, 새로운 문제 유형 등에 익숙해지는 훈련을 할 필요가 있다.)

Use as a Compass for Success in Rolling Admissions (수시 전형 합격 위한 나침반 활용)

Re-takers (N-sus) do not take the March academic assessment, and some elective subjects in the math section are excluded from the scope. Additionally, since there's still a long time until the CSAT, it's hard to see it as a test that precisely identifies your objective position. Nevertheless, it's worth doing a mid-term check by comparing your scores from the academic assessment with your grades 1–2 school record subject scores to see which admissions track is advantageous for applying to your desired university. (3월 학평은 N수생들이 응시하지 않고, 수학 영역에서 선택 과목의 출제 범위도 일부 제외된다. 또한, 수능까지 아직 많은 시간이 남아 있어 자신의 객관적인 위치를 정확히 파악할 수 있는 시험이라고 보기에는 한계가 있다. 그럼에도 학평에서 얻은 자신의 점수와 1, 2학년 학생부 교과 성적을 비교해보면서 희망 대학을 지원하기 위해 어떤 전형이 유리한지 중간 점검을 해볼 필요는 있다.)

Director Woo Yeon-cheol said, "If your regular school grades are usually better than your academic assessment scores, it's better to focus more on preparing for the midterms and finals in the first semester of 3rd grade." He added, "If the school record-based admissions track at the university you're applying to applies a minimum CSAT score requirement, you shouldn't neglect managing your grades by CSAT subject to meet that criterion." (우연철 소장은 “평소 교과 성적이 학평 성적보다 잘 나오는 경우라면 3학년 1학기 중간·기말 고사 대비에 좀더 집중하는 것이 좋다”며 “만약 지원하려는 대학의 학생부 교과전형이 수능 최저학력기준을 적용하고 있다면 기준 충족을 위해 수능 영역별 등급 관리 또한 소홀히 해서는 안 된다”고 말했다.)

Kim Byeong-jin, director of Etus Education Evaluation Research Institute, advised, "It's necessary to use the academic assessment focusing on the level of completion of what you studied during winter vacation. For example, you should establish future study plans around problems you thought you had studied enough for but got wrong in practice." He added, "Furthermore, if you have the rolling admissions minimum CSAT score requirement in mind, setting required grades by subject, checking how many more correct answers you need, and then establishing study plans is also a good method." (김병진 이투스 교육평가연구소장은 “겨울 방학 동안 학습했던 내용의 학습 완성도를 중심으로 학력평가를 활용할 필요가 있다. 일례로 학습을 충분히 했다고 생각했으나 실전에서 틀리는 문제를 중심으로 이후의 학습 계획을 수립해야 한다”며 “나아가 수시 수능최저학력기준을 염두에 두고 있는 경우 영역별 필요 등급을 설정해 두고 몇 문제가 더 필요한지를 살펴 이후 학습 계획을 수립하는 것도 좋은 방법”이라고 조언했다.)

If you're a student lacking CSAT competitiveness, you should establish support strategies to actively utilize other admissions factors such as essay tests or practical exams. (만약, 수능 경쟁력이 부족한 학생이라면 논술, 실기 등 다른 전형요소를 적극 활용할 수 있도록 지원 전략을 수립해야 한다.)

Must Establish Phased Study Plans Until the CSAT (수능 때까지 시기별 학습계획 세워야)

The most important thing is to identify weak subjects based on the March academic assessment results by subject, consider how to supplement them, and set concrete long-term goals and plans to improve CSAT scores. Rather than dwelling on the results, you should treat it as a stepping stone for a new start, objectively grasping your abilities and weaknesses. Even if your scores come out differently than expected, you should adopt the mindset of gaining real exam experience, set target CSAT scores and grades, and use it as foundational data for designing study plans by CSAT subject for the remaining period and for setting the direction of college prep. (가장 중요한 건 3월 학평 과목별 결과를 토대로 취약과목을 파악, 이를 보완할 방법을 고민하는 한편 수능 성적 향상을 위한 장기 목표와 계획을 구체적으로 설정하는 것이다. 시험 결과에 연연하기보다는 자신의 실력과 취약점을 객관적으로 파악하는 등 새로운 출발을 하는 디딤돌로 삼아야 한다. 성적이 기대와 다르게 나왔다 하더라도 실전 경험을 쌓는다는 생각을 갖고 수능 목표 점수와 등급을 정하고 남은 기간 수능 영역별 학습 계획을 세우는 근거 자료와 입시 준비 방향을 설계하는 기초 자료로 활용해야 한다.)

Director Woo Yeon-cheol said, "If your academic assessment scores come out higher than your efforts suggest, rather than becoming overconfident, you need to check whether you solved problems with a complete understanding of concepts and accurately knew the intent behind the questions before moving on—only then can you minimize mistakes on the actual CSAT." (우연철 소장은 “학평 성적이 자신의 노력에 비해 높게 나왔을 경우 의기양양해하기보다는 완벽한 개념 이해와 더불어 출제 의도를 정확하게 알고 풀었던 것인지 체크하고 넘어가야 실제 수능에서 실수를 최소화할 수 있다”고 말했다.)

If, unfortunately, your scores came out worse than expected, the priority is to clearly identify the causes of the wrong answers. Rather than being impatient, you need to set study strategies and plans focused on future mock exams and the CSAT with the mindset of gradually reducing mistakes through concept organization until the CSAT. (안타깝게도 자신이 예상했던 것보다 성적이 잘 나오지 않은 학생이라면 틀린 문제의 원인을 명확히 파악하는 것이 우선이다. 조급한 마음보다는 개념 정리를 통해 수능 전까지 실수를 점차 줄여나가겠다는 생각을 가지고 앞으로 몇 차례 더 치르게 될 모의고사와 수능에 초점을 맞춰 학습 전략과 계획을 세울 필요가 있다.)

Director Kim Byeong-jin advised, "Even if it's tough, you must definitely review the test process and all subject questions on the day the exam ends, analyzing overall question patterns, high-scoring items, and incorrect answers." He added, "Especially for wrong problems, rather than just checking the correct answer, it's good to organize in detail the reason for the mistake, the accurate problem-solving method, the scope of the question, and related concepts, and check them regularly." (김병진 소장은 “힘들더라도 반드시 시험이 끝난 당일 시험 과정, 전 과목 문제를 복기하며 전반적인 출제 유형, 고득점 문항, 오답 분석을 해야 한다”며 “특히 틀린 문제는 단순히 정답만 확인하는 것이 아니라 틀린 이유와 정확한 문제풀이 방법, 문항 출제 범위 및 관련 개념 등을 상세히 정리해 수시로 확인하는 것이 좋다”고 조언했다.)

If you haven't yet met the minimum CSAT score requirement demanded by your desired university, or if your academic assessment scores are generally better than your school record grades and you're considering regular admissions as your main track, then the academic assessment and subsequent mock evaluations are truly stepping-stone opportunities to raise your grades. Based on results by subject, you should identify your weak subjects, consider how to supplement them, and set concrete long-term goals and plans to improve CSAT scores. (희망 대학에서 요구하는 수능 최저학력기준을 아직 충족하지 못했거나 학생부 교과 성적보다 학평 성적이 대체로 더 잘 나와 정시를 주력 전형으로 고려하고 있는 수험생이라면 학평과 이후 모의평가는 그야말로 등급을 올릴 수 있는 디딤돌 같은 기회다. 과목별 결과를 토대로 자신의 취약과목을 파악하고 앞으로 어떻게 보완할지 고민하는 등 수능 성적 향상을 위한 장기 목표와 계획을 구체적으로 설정해야 한다.)

Lee Chi-woo, director of Visang Education Admissions Evaluation Institute, said, "You should set target CSAT scores and grades and use the results as foundational data for establishing study plans by CSAT subject for the remaining period." He emphasized that it's important to check how much you need to improve to enter your target university and, based on results by subject and area, establish phased study plans until the CSAT. (이치우 비상교육 입시평가연구소장은 “수능 목표 점수와 등급을 정하고, 남은 기간 수능 영역별 학습 계획을 세우기 위한 근거 자료로 활용해야 한다”고 말했다. 자신이 목표로 한 대학에 입학하기 위해 어느 정도까지 성적을 향상해야 하는지 점검하고, 영역·과목별 성적 결과를 바탕으로 수능 때까지 시기별 학습계획을 세우는 것이 중요하다는 것이다.)

Prepare Considering the CSAT Subject Reflection of Your Desired University (희망 대학 수능 반영(과목) 영역 대비)

Starting with the March academic assessment through to the CSAT on November 19, establishing a long-term strategic study plan is paramount. During the first semester, study centered on the CSAT subject areas reflected by your desired university, and carefully check weighted subject areas to differentiate study emphasis. Setting and executing concrete daily or weekly study plans by subject and area is helpful. Using academic assessment and CSAT mock exam workbooks, identify weak units and evaluation areas by subject, then select one self-study book or reference book per subject along with EBS CSAT Essentials materials and study each at least twice repeatedly—this is recommended. (3월 학평을 시작으로 오는 11월19일 수능시험까지 장기간 전략적인 공부 계획을 세우는 것이 무엇보다 중요하다. 1학기 동안에는 희망 대학 수능 반영 영역(과목)을 중심으로 공부하되, 가중치 부여 영역(과목) 등을 꼼꼼히 챙겨 공부 비중을 달리할 필요가 있다. 영역·과목별로 구체적인 일일 또는 주간 학습계획을 세워 실천하는 것이 도움이 된다. 학평과 수능 모의평가 문제집 등을 통해 영역(과목)별 부족한 단원과 평가 영역 등을 파악한 뒤 영역(과목)별로 EBS 수능특강 교재와 함께 자신에게 맞는 자습서 또는 참고서를 1권씩 선정해 최소 2회 정도 반복 학습하는 것을 추천한다.)

Director Woo Yeon-cheol advised, "Based on the March academic assessment results by subject, you should identify your weak subjects, consider how to supplement them, and set concrete long-term goals and plans to improve CSAT scores." He added, "After taking mock exams, analyze the causes of incorrect answers, retry wrong problems, and if you don't understand something, actively refer to textbooks. Especially if you have many wrong answers, rather than just solving problems, you need to rebuild your foundation by relearning concepts from the start." (우연철 소장은 “3월 학평 과목별 결과를 토대로 자신의 취약과목을 파악하고 앞으로 어떻게 보완할지 고민하는 등 수능 성적 향상을 위한 장기 목표와 계획을 구체적으로 설정해야 한다”며 “모의고사를 본 이후에는 오답의 원인을 분석해 틀린 문제는 다시 풀어보고, 이해가 되지 않는다면 교과서 등을 적극 참고해야 한다. 특히 오답이 많다면 문제풀이만 할 것이 아니라 개념 이해부터 다시 학습하는 등 기초를 다질 필요가 있다”고 조언했다.)

In this regard, Lee Man-gi, director of Uway Education Evaluation Research Institute, proposed the following subject-specific study strategies until the CSAT: "For Korean, focus on improving reading comprehension, but before that, you need an accurate understanding of the beginning of texts or sentences and the answer choices. For math, intensively study weak units or question types, and when solving problems, check whether you've missed any concepts. For English, rather than solving many problems from March onward, use past exam questions to identify wrong answers in high-difficulty question types and avoid repeating the same mistakes. For social/science studies, not only the basic principles in EBS CSAT textbooks but also materials such as figures, photos, and charts are highly likely to appear in similar forms, so you should pay close attention to them." (이와 관련해 이만기 유웨이 교육평가연구소장은 수능 때까지 과목별 학습 전략을 다음과 같이 제안했다. “국어는 본문 독해력을 키우는 데 주력하되, 그 전에 글이나 문장의 첫머리, 답지에 대한 정확한 이해가 필요하다. 수학은 취약단원이나 유형을 집중적으로 공부하되, 문제를 풀 때는 놓친 개념이 있는지 확인해야 한다. 영어는 3월부터 많은 문제를 풀기보다는 기출문제를 이용해 난도 높은 유형에서의 오답을 확인하고 같은 실수를 반복하지 않도록 해야 한다. 탐구는 EBS 수능교재에 나와 있는 기본 원리뿐 아니라 그림, 사진, 도표 등 자료 또한 유사하게 출제될 가능성이 높으므로 이를 잘 봐야 한다.”)

Meanwhile, this year's academic assessments hosted by city and provincial offices of education will be held four times in total: March 24, followed by May 7 (Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education), July 8 (Incheon Metropolitan Office of Education), and October 20 (Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education). The mock evaluations administered by KICE, which oversees the CSAT, will be held twice—on June 4 and September 2—and since both current seniors and graduates take them together, they offer the most accurate prediction of your score on the actual CSAT on November 19. (한편, 올해 시도교육청이 주관하는 학평은 3월24일에 이어 5월7일(경기도교육청), 7월8일(인천시교육청), 10월20일(서울시교육청) 등 총 4번 실시된다. 수능을 주관하는 한국교육과정평가원에서 시행하는 모의평가는 6월4일과 9월2일 두 번 치러지는데, 고3 수험생은 물론 졸업생도 함께 치르기 때문에 11월19일 치러질 실제 수능에서 본인의 성적을 가장 정확하게 예측해볼 수 있다.)

Reporter Kim Mi-young kimmy@hani.co.kr (김미영 기자 kimmy@hani.co.kr)

item.title: "Shall We Look for Green Seasonal Ingredients Today?" (“오늘은 초록색 제철 재료를 찾아볼까”)
item.description:
"Seasonal core" is trending. It refers to a lifestyle of seeking out and eating foods that are in season, making a point to go out and see flowers that bloom for their brief season, and enjoying activities aligned with the 24 solar terms. This trend, which has spread among the younger generation in their 20s and 30s, is actually even more essential for children. Raised amid supermarkets where strawberries are available all year round and indoor lifestyles that operate regardless of the weather, children are more likely to learn about seasonal changes with their heads rather than their bodies. This is why firsthand experiences of tasting seasonal foods and feeling the solar terms on their skin are all the more necessary. Here, we introduce tips for teaching solar terms in everyday life that awaken children's sensitivity to the seasons. <<> Learning the Senses of the Seasons Through Taste <<> The easiest and most powerful way to teach solar terms begins at the dining table. Rather than big-box supermarkets, try visiting traditional markets or local food direct-sale outlets with your child. In spring, let them smell the slightly bitter aroma of shepherd's purse and wild chives; in summer, let them touch the deep green young plums with their hands—these experiences themselves are living lessons. <<> When you go to the market, don't just stop at grocery shopping—give your child a small mission. You can issue color-based missions like, "Today, let's find yellow seasonal ingredients," or have them ask the elderly vendors directly about the names of vegetables they've never seen before. Through brief conversations with unfamiliar adults, children naturally gain vivid knowledge about seasonal foods along with valuable social experiences. <<> Serving foods suited to each solar term at the table is also a great approach. On Daeboreum (the first full moon of the lunar year), eat five-grain rice and seasoned vegetables together while cracking nuts for good luck; on Dongji (winter solstice), boil red bean porridge and start a conversation like, "They say today is the longest night of the year—why do you think that is?" No elaborate explanations are needed; a single short conversation over the meal is the most natural way to make solar terms memorable. <<> Involving children in the cooking process is also beneficial. In spring, make jam while plucking strawberry stems or prepare spring cabbage bibimbap; in summer, cut up watermelon to make fruit punch; in autumn, peel persimmons and hang them under the eaves to observe the process of them becoming dried persimmons. In winter, gather the whole family to make kimchi or soak red beans and boil porridge. Through tastes and activities that change with each season, you can naturally awaken a sense of the seasons. <<> Fun Solar Term Activities to Enjoy in Daily Life <<> Solar terms were once the foundation of an agrarian society, but for modern children, they can become the basis for delightful seasonal play. For example, on Ipbun (February 4), which marks the beginning of spring, you can write the characters "입춘대길" (Ipchun Daegil, wishing for great luck in the new year) in Chinese characters or color them in and post them around the house. The upcoming Gogu (April 20) is the solar term when spring rain nourishes all grains. As the full farming season begins, plant seeds in a flowerpot and start a seed growth journal. Children can draw and record what seeds were planted and when and how much water was given. <<> In summer, there are Haji and Daeseo. Haji (June 21) is the longest day of the year. On this day, stick a stick into the ground with your child to measure the length of its shadow, recording it in the morning, at noon, and in the evening. This creates a fascinating science lesson where children can see with their own eyes how the sun's position changes. Daeseo (July 23) is the hottest period. Sharing stories about how ancestors ate samgyetang and soaked their feet in streams to ward off the heat, try making refreshing seasonal foods together like watermelon punch or cucumber cold soup. On Chubun (September 23), record the time the sun sets together, and in the following days, observe the sunset times to experience the days growing longer. The fact that this is the day when day and night are balanced becomes an amazing discovery for children. <<> Keeping up with solar terms in this way is, in itself, a small event that enriches daily life. If you step away from the educational perspective and turn it into a family activity of joyfully celebrating seasonal foods, children will come to look forward to solar terms and observe them with anticipation and curiosity. <<> Cultivating Seasonal Awareness Through Reading and Recording <<> Adding picture books to solar term activities connects experiences with language. "Solar Term Magic" (written by Cheon Mi-jin, illustrated by Min Seung-ji) is a picture book that warmly unfolds the 24 solar terms through the four seasons of a family that moves to a rural home. It shows children, at their eye level, that solar terms are not grand concepts but a joyful rhythm that enriches everyday life. "The 24 Solar Terms Picture Book at a Glance" (written by Ji Ho-jin, illustrated by Lee Hyeok) weaves all 24 solar terms from Ipbun to Daehan into engaging stories and illustrations. It includes the meanings and origins behind each solar term's name, the natural phenomena that occur during each period, and the wisdom of ancestors in applying solar terms to farming and daily routines. <<> Adding records to reading deepens seasonal awareness even further. Choose a neighborhood walking path with your child, and whenever the solar terms change, take photos at the same spot or jot down changes in colors and scents. Pick a tree near home that you like and observe it throughout the entire year. From budding leaves to blooming flowers, autumn foliage, and bare branches, recording that process will become a more vivid natural textbook than any science book after a year. If your child is still learning to write, drawing with colors and shapes is more than enough. <<> If you want to start lightly, hanging a calendar on the wall featuring the 24 solar terms or seasonal foods is a good option. When your child starts looking at the calendar on their own, asking, "What's the next solar term? What do we eat then?"—you've already half-succeeded at solar term education. If you want to go one step further, try making a "season box" with your child. It's an activity where you prepare a small box for each season and collect natural objects that can only be found during that time. In the spring box, press-dried cherry blossom petals or sprouting seeds; in the summer box, seashells picked up at the beach or cicada shells; in the autumn box, acorns and maple leaves; and in the winter box, dried tangerine peels. <<> Solar term education is not about memorization but about experiences in daily life. It's okay not to know the names of the terms. A simple remark like, "Don't you think the air smells like spring now?" or "The days are getting longer than last month, aren't they?" starts a conversation that awakens a child's seasonal sensitivity. Pick one activity per season to make daily life a little richer. After a year of this, before you know it, your child will grow into one who says first, "I think summer is coming soon." <<> Park Eun-ah, Contributing Writer (‘제철 코어'가 유행이다. 그 계절에 나는 음식을 찾아 먹고, 한철 피는 꽃을 보러 일부러 길을 나서고, 24기 절기에 맞는 활동을 즐기는 삶의 방식을 뜻한다. 2030 젊은 세대 사이에서 번진 이 유행은 사실 아이들에게 더 절실하다. 사계절 내내 딸기가 팔리는 마트, 날씨와 무관하게 돌아가는 실내 생활 속에서 자라는 아이들은 계절의 변화를 몸이 아닌 머리로 배우기 쉽다. 제철과 절기를 직접 맛보고 피부로 느끼는 경험이 더욱 필요한 이유다. 아이의 계절 감수성을 깨우는 일상 속 절기 교육 노하우를 소개한다.)

item.title: Curiosity About History, Deepened by 'The King and the Clown' — Let's Explore Further (‘왕과 사는 남자’로 깊어진 역사 호기심 더 키워볼까)
item.description:
An unexpected phenomenon has occurred as the film "The King and the Clown" became a box-office hit. Audiences leaving theaters began heading to Yeongwol, Gangwon Province. Cheongnyeongpo, where King Danjong was exiled, and Jangneung saw far more visitors than usual, and online searches about the real history of Danjong and Eom Heung-do surged. A single historical film or a single comic book can serve as a more powerful and engaging history teacher than any textbook. Here, we've gathered ways to teach history in everyday life, from historical content worth watching with children to tips on connecting it with historical field trips. <<> Encountering History Through Film and Drama Stories <<> Among films and dramas, there are countless works set against real historical backdrops. Simply watching such works tailored to a child's age or school curriculum becomes a valuable form of indirect experience. The moment a figure reduced to a single line in a textbook comes alive on screen, history begins to feel entirely different. <<> For young children and elementary schoolers, the animated series "K-Pop Demon Hunters," which gained explosive popularity last year, is a great starting point. Set in the modern era but infused with Korean traditional culture throughout, the show revolves around the K-pop girl group Huntrix, who secretly work as demon hunters protecting the world. While watching, look for elements of Korean folk belief such as the grim reaper, dokkaebi, and magpie tigers, as well as traditional symbols like hanbok, hanok, and Seoul landmarks. Asking questions like "What's the name of that weapon that character is holding?" or "That building looks familiar—where have we seen it?" is enough to spark an engaging journey into history. <<> For upper elementary students and beyond, more in-depth historical content is worth exploring. For example, the film "The Throne" portrays the story of King Yeongjo and Crown Prince Sado with a focus on the characters' perspectives, making it ideal for examining the human emotions and dilemmas behind historical events. Other notable films include "The Admiral: Roaring Currents," which depicts the naval battles of the Imjin War; "The Astronomer: Ask the Stars," about King Sejong and Jang Yeong-sil; "The Fortress," set during the Manchu invasion of 1636; and "Dongju: The Portrait of a Poet," which portrays the Japanese colonial period through the story of poet Yun Dong-ju. <<> After watching such content, looking up additional information about the characters can deepen the lingering impression. It's also important to explore together where historical facts and cinematic imagination diverge. Especially from upper elementary school onward, children begin to develop the cognitive ability to distinguish between staged portrayals and actual facts, so it's beneficial to pair this with media literacy training that encourages critical reception of content. <<> For children of the video generation, YouTube is also a highly accessible learning tool. The key is choosing the right channels. EBS's "History Channel e" is a program that stylishly reinterprets key scenes and events in Korean history in short episodes of around five minutes each. It's well-suited to children's attention spans and can be searched by topic on the EBS website and YouTube channel. Dasan Books' culture channel "Gyoyang Mandu" tackles intriguing historical questions like "How did kings use the restroom during the Joseon Dynasty?" with charming illustrations and humor, offering a light and fun way to approach history. <<> Starting History Through the Joy of Reading <<> The most familiar way to study history is, of course, through books. For children who find history difficult or are younger, starting with comic books is a great option. In the early grades when children first encounter history, it's better to focus on gripping stories centered on specific figures or events rather than chronological learning. <<> "Mr. Dragon's Lively Korean History" (Sahoepyeongnon) is a series that has long held its place as essential reading for history learning. Using a storytelling format where the character Mr. Dragon travels through historical sites with children, it allows readers to naturally follow the long arc from prehistoric times to the modern era as if it were a tale. The authors personally visited cultural heritage sites in 37 major cities across the country, covering over 200 locations, and their on-site lectures highlighting key points can also be viewed via QR code videos. <<> If a child has begun to take an interest in history comics, books like "Seol Min-seok's Korean History Adventure" (Dankkum Ai) are also excellent choices. An animated version based on the same content is available, allowing books and videos to be used together. <<> For children in middle school and above, reading historical novels together and discussing them can be rewarding. A notable example is Han Kang's "Human Acts" (Changbi), which won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Literature. Set against the Gwangju Uprising of May 18, 1980, the novel vividly portrays the figures who fought against martial law forces and the stories of those left behind. It allows readers to experience tragic modern history not as a mere textbook event but as the stories of living people. After reading, visiting the National May 18 Democracy Cemetery or the May 18 Archives in Gwangju connects the story in the book to living history. <<> Author Lee Geum-yi's "Aloha, My Mothers" is set in Hawai'i during the Japanese colonial period and tells the story of first-generation overseas Koreans and the women who married them and built their lives together. The author, long beloved as a leading voice in young adult literature, is known for weaving historical facts into the warm stories of her characters. <<> History Outings Connected to Content <<> Interest sparked by content becomes more deeply ingrained when it leads to historical sites. After watching a drama or film, a simple comment like "That scene's backdrop is a real place—shall we go see it?" creates exciting motivation for a child. For instance, after watching "The Fortress," you could walk the trails of Namhansanseong, or after "Resistance: The Story of Yu Gwan-sun," visit the Seodaemun Prison History Hall. When content and real sites are linked like this, a child recalls scenes from the film at every stone wall and exhibit, absorbing history with a completely different level of depth. <<> When arriving at the site, it's important not to leave the child as a passive observer. Before visiting a historical location featured in a film, set a mission together. Simple challenges like "Find the spot most resembling a scene from the movie" or "Look for an exhibit that appeared in the drama" turn a potentially dull visit into an exciting adventure. For a more active approach, children can become guides themselves, explaining the site to their guardians in a "one-day curator" activity. By researching related content in advance and having the child explain on-site, they gain both a sense of accomplishment and learning benefits. <<> Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung in Seoul are prime examples of accessible historical destinations. These two palaces, backdrops to countless historical dramas, can naturally be visited after watching any Joseon-era drama or film. If you've just seen content about the independence movement, head to the Seodaemun Prison History Hall or the Ahn Jung-geun Memorial Museum on Namsan. <<> History Education You Can Use at Home Right Away <<> The best way to use content in history education is simpler than you might think. Just one question after a film or drama ends is enough. A light question like "Which character from today stood out to you the most?" or "What kind of life do you think you'd have lived if you'd been born in that era?" plants a seed of historical imagination in a child's mind. Guardians don't need to feel pressured to know all the historical facts. What matters more is the attitude of being curious and searching for answers together. <<> After consuming content, activities that follow while emotions are still fresh are most effective. Writing a brief reflection as a drawing or a few lines of text works well. If writing feels difficult, simply prompting speech with something like "Want to say something to one of the characters you saw today?" is more than enough. <<> There's one essential point to keep in mind. Historical dramas and films blend factual events with fiction. To prevent a child from taking everything in a drama as absolute truth, build the habit after watching of exploring together: "Is this scene real history, or a story the writer imagined?" Clearly pointing out that "dramas add imagination for entertainment, and the actual records say this" naturally teaches children to critically accept information. Over time, this process cultivates not only historical knowledge but also a discerning eye for media. <<> Park Eun-ah, Contributing Reporter (영화 ‘왕과 사는 남자’가 흥행하면서 뜻밖의 현상이 일어났다. 극장을 나온 관객들이 강원도 영월로 향하기 시작한 것이다. 단종이 유배됐던 청령포와 장릉에는 평소보다 훨씬 많은 방문객이 찾았고, 단종과 엄흥도의 실제 역사를 찾아보는 검색량도 치솟았다. 역사를 다룬 영화 한 편, 만화책 한 권이 어떤 교과서보다 강력하고 흥미로운 역사 선생님이 될 수 있다. 아이와 함께 볼 만한 역사 콘텐츠부터 역사 기행과 연결하는 방법까지, 일상에서 시도해볼 수 있는 역사 교육 방법을 모아 봤다.)

item.title: "We will nurture 'AI leaders with virtue (Deokseong)'" (“‘덕성(德性) 갖춘 AI 리더’ 길러내겠다”)
item.description:
What kind of talent is needed in an era where artificial intelligence (AI) finds the answers? As AI reshapes the order of society at large, corporate hiring standards are also changing. While academic background and knowledge have mattered up until now, there is a view that in the AI era, communication skills—the ability to think and collaborate alongside machines—will become increasingly important. With the advent of AI, rather than talent built on rote memorization, individuals who freely express their thoughts and perspectives while placing importance on morality, ethics, and the public good will be in the spotlight. (인공지능(AI)이 답을 찾아주는 시대에는 어떤 인재가 필요할까. 인공지능이 사회 전반의 질서를 재편하면서 기업의 인재 채용 기준도 변화하고 있다. 지금까지는 학력과 지식이 좌우했다면, AI 시대의 인재는 기계와 함께 생각하고 협력하는 소통능력이 중요해질 것이라는 의견이 나온다. 인공지능의 등장으로, 많이 외워 만들어진 인재보다는 학생들의 생각과 관점을 자유롭게 표현하되 도덕과 윤리, 공공성을 중시하는 인재가 각광받을 것이라는 의미다.)

This is why Min Jae-hong, President of Duksung Women's University, emphasized upon taking office last February: "AI and digital transformation are already a reality," adding, "We will build an AI-based university where technological efficiency and human values are in balance—one that reflects together on 'ethics, publicness, responsibility, and human dignity.'" (민재홍 덕성여대 총장이 지난 2월 취임하면서 “AI·디지털 전환은 이미 현실이 됐다”며 “기술의 효율성과 인간의 가치가 균형을 이루는, 즉 ‘윤리·공공성·책임성·인간의 존엄성’을 함께 성찰하는 AI 기반 대학으로 만들겠다”고 강조한 이유다.)

In this regard, President Min has set Duksung's direction as 'X+AI' rather than 'AI+X'. This means that AI is not the master; rather, each major (X) is the center, and AI serves as the wings that expand the capabilities of that major. This philosophy extends the spirit of self-reliance, self-sufficiency, and self-awareness of the founder, Cha Mirisa, into the AI era, and is designed to lead to the cultivation of 'virtuous (Deokseong) AI leaders.' (이와 관련해 민 총장은 덕성의 방향을 ‘AI+X’보다 ‘X+AI’로 설정했다. AI가 주인이 아니라 각 전공(X)이 중심이고, AI는 그 전공의 역량을 확장하는 날개가 되어야 한다는 뜻이다. 이 철학은 설립자인 차미리사 선생의 자생·자립·자각 정신을 AI 시대에 맞게 확장한 것으로 ‘덕성(德性) AI 리더’ 양성으로 이어지도록 설계한 것이다.)

We spoke with President Min Jae-hong about the direction Duksung Women's University should take in these rapidly changing times, its goals and philosophy for talent development, and his aspirations as president. (민재홍 총장에게 급변하는 시대에 덕성여대가 나아가야 할 방향과 인재양성 목표와 철학, 총장으로서의 포부 등을 들어봤다.)

–It has been just over a month since you took office as the 13th president. How do you feel? (–13대 총장으로 취임한 지 한 달 남짓 지났다. 소감은.)

"The past month was not a time for 'greetings' but a time for 'review.' Since taking office, I quickly identified where Duksung's education, research, and administration are stuck, and where students feel inconveniences, and I am preparing to execute the promises I made. Above all, since we are in an era of digital revolution where AI is the dominant trend, I intend to prioritize the reorganization of the educational system. Through the establishment of an AI-based personalized platform that connects everything from 'course registration – grades – campus life – counseling – employment and career,' and the development of courses and curricula where AI is integrated into all majors, I will achieve educational innovation that students can feel and connect it to employment." (“지난 한 달은 ‘인사’의 시간이 아니라 ‘점검’의 시간이었다. 취임 이후 덕성의 교육·연구·행정이 어떤 지점에서 막히고, 학생들이 어디에서 불편을 체감하는지부터 빠르게 확인했고, 공약했던 내용들을 실행하기 위한 준비를 하고 있다. 무엇보다 AI가 대세가 된 디지털 혁명시대인 만큼 교육체계 개편을 우선적으로 실행하려고 한다. ‘수강신청-성적-학교생활-상담-취업·진로’까지 하나로 연결되는 AI 기반 맞춤형 플랫폼 구축, 모든 전공에 AI가 접목되는 교과목 및 커리큘럼 개발을 통해 학생들이 체감하는 교육혁신을 이뤄내, 취업으로 연결될 수 있게 하겠다.”)

–You have said that you will make Duksung Women's University a university that nurtures new innovative talent, like the prestigious women's colleges Wellesley College and Smith College. In this regard, you have emphasized the 'Duksung AI Initiative.' What is its core? (–총장께서는 덕성여대를 여성 명문 대학인 웰즐리 칼리지(Wellesley College), 스미스 칼리지(Smith College)처럼 새로운 혁신의 인재를 길러내는 대학으로 만들겠다고 했다. 이와 관련해 ‘덕성 AI 이니셔티브’를 강조했는데, 핵심은.)

"The 'Duksung AI Initiative' is a transformation into an AI-based university where technological efficiency and human values are in balance. We will introduce AI across education, research, and administration, while simultaneously promoting reflection on ethics, publicness, responsibility, and human dignity. Duksung's AI transformation must be human-centered, not technology-centered. We will build an AI-era education where majors are not excluded and human intelligence is not alienated, developing the university into a sustainable, future-oriented institution where all members grow together." (“‘덕성 AI 이니셔티브’는 기술 효율성과 인간 가치가 균형을 이루는 AI 기반 대학 전환이다. AI를 교육·연구·행정 전반에 도입하고, 동시에 윤리·공공성·책임성, 인간 존엄성에 대한 성찰도 함께 추진하겠다. 덕성의 AI 전환은 기술 중심이 아니라 사람 중심이어야 한다. 전공이 배제되지 않고 인간의 지능이 소외되지 않는 AI 시대 교육을 구축해 모든 구성원이 함께 성장하는 지속가능한 미래형 대학으로 발전시켜나가겠다.”)

–As a women's university, what is Duksung's role in the AI era? (–여성대학으로서 AI 시대에 ‘덕성’의 역할은.)

"I believe that in the AI era, a university must go beyond simply 'teaching technology' and also cultivate the judgment (ethics, publicness, critical thinking) needed to use technology responsibly. Based on our identity as an 'educational community that transforms women's potential into social value,' nurturing female leaders essential for the AI era—those equipped with ethics, publicness, and critical thinking—is Duksung's role and the path to realizing the 'prestigious Duksung.'" (“AI 시대 대학은 단순히 기술을 ‘가르치는 곳’을 넘어, 기술을 책임 있게 활용할 수 있는 판단력(윤리·공공성·비판적 사고)을 함께 길러야 한다고 생각한다. ‘여성의 잠재력을 사회적 가치로 전환시키는 교육 공동체’라는 정체성을 바탕으로, 윤리·공공성·비판적 사고를 갖춘 AI 시대에 꼭 필요한 여성 리더를 길러내는 것이 덕성의 역할이자, ‘명문 덕성’을 구현해내는 길이라고 생각한다. ”)

–If you were to describe the talent Duksung aims to cultivate in one sentence. (–덕성이 길러내고자 하는 인재를 한 문장으로 말한다면.)

"'AI leaders with virtue (Deokseong).' They are not people who 'use technology well,' but people who can read the limitations and biases of technology and judge social responsibility alongside it. In other words, they are creative, convergent AI talents equipped with humanities and social imagination, scientific and technological creativity, and artistic and cultural sensibilities." (“‘덕성(德性)을 갖춘 AI 리더’다. 기술을 ‘잘 쓰는 사람’이 아니라, 기술의 한계·편향을 읽고 사회적 책임을 함께 판단하는 사람이다. 즉, 인문사회학적 상상력, 과학기술 창조력, 예술문화 감각을 갖춘 창의융합형 AI 인재다.”)

–What are the specific action plans for nurturing 'AI leaders with virtue'? (–‘덕성 갖춘 AI 리더’ 양성을 위한 구체적인 실천방안은.)

"It's not about 'AI for specific advanced departments only,' but about 'establishing basic competencies for all students + deepened competencies per major + an educational support system.' To this end, we will make basic AI competencies mandatory for all students ('Computational Thinking' → 'Duksung AI Literacy'), and the 'AI Convergence Education Support Center' will provide standardized AI-Wing lecture plans and practice materials ('meal kits'), AI TA matching, and even support for students' AI subscriptions (e.g., paid ChatGPT versions/credits). In short, it can be summarized as: △Making AI literacy mandatory for all students △Expanding X+AI courses for each major △The AI-Wing (standard lecture plans/practice) and AI TA system △Industry-academia linked projects (e.g., AI new drug and biohealth clusters), etc." (“‘특정 첨단학과만의 AI’가 아니라, ‘전교생 기본 역량 + 전공별 심화 역량 + 교육지원 체계를 구축’하는 것이다. 이를 위해 전교생 AI 기초 역량을 필수화하고(‘컴퓨팅사고’ → ‘덕성 AI 리터러시’), ‘AI 융합교육 지원센터’에서 표준화된 AI-Wing 강의안·실습자료(‘밀키트’) 제공, AI TA 매칭, 학생들의 AI 구독(예: ChatGPT 유료 버전/크레딧) 지원까지 연결할 것이다. 간단히 말하면, △전교생 AI 리터러시 필수화 △전공별 X+AI 교과 확대 △AI-Wing(표준 강의안·실습)과 AI TA 체계 △산학 연계형 프로젝트(예: AI 신약·바이오헬스 클러스터 등) 등으로 요약할 수 있겠다.”)

–What are Duksung Women's University's unique strengths, and how do you plan to develop them? (–덕성여대만의 강점은 무엇이고, 이를 어떻게 키워나갈 계획인지.)

"People often misunderstand that a women's university focuses mainly on humanities and social sciences. However, our university has various humanities and social science majors such as Early Childhood Education, Art History, and Cultural Anthropology, as well as science and technology-related majors including five tracks within Digital Software Engineering, Bioengineering, Food and Nutrition, Chemistry, and Information Statistics. Furthermore, the College of Future Talent houses 'advanced' departments such as the Department of AI New Drugs, the Department of Data Science, and the Department of Virtual Reality Convergence. In other words, our strength is that we don't concentrate 'advanced' fields into specific departments; rather, the entire group of majors—science and technology, data, content, bio, etc.—shares AI as a basic competency. To support this, we will establish an 'AI Convergence Education Support Center' to provide AI-Wing lecture plans, practice templates, and evaluation criteria that can be immediately applied to major courses, AI TA matching, and support for student AI subscriptions, thereby raising the quality of instruction and practice in advanced majors. On the employment front, we will meticulously design work experience and industry-academia connections—such as major-specific employment support (responding to company-specific hiring processes), expanding the field practice semester system and Duksung Internship, AI convergence job and startup fairs, and the Dobong-Duksung Job and Startup Festival—to produce tangible results." (“여대라고 하면 인문사회계열 위주의 대학이라고 오해한다. 하지만 우리 대학은 유아교육, 미술사학, 문화인류학 등 다양한 인문사회계열 전공 외에도 디지털소프트웨어공학 내 5개 트랙, 바이오공학, 식품영양학, 화학, 정보통계학 등 과학기술 관련 전공이 있다. 또한 미래인재대학에 AI신약학과, 데이터사이언스학과, 가상현실융합학과 등 ‘첨단’학과도 포진해 있다. 즉, 특정 학과에 ‘첨단’을 몰아주는 방식이 아니라 과학기술·데이터·콘텐츠·바이오 등 전공군 전체가 AI를 기본 역량으로 공유하는 구조가 갖춰져 있다는 것이 강점이다. 이를 뒷받침하기 위해 ‘AI 융합교육 지원센터’를 만들어 전공 수업에 바로 적용 가능한 AI-Wing 강의안·실습 템플릿·평가기준 제공, AI TA 매칭, 학생 AI 구독 지원 등을 추진해 첨단 전공의 수업·실습 품질을 끌어올리겠다. 취업 측면에서는 전공 맞춤형 취업지원(기업별 채용 절차 대응), 현장실습학기제·덕성인턴십 확대, AI 융합 취·창업박람회, 도봉-덕성 취창업 페스티벌 등 일경험·산학 연결을 촘촘히 설계해 성과를 만들어가겠다.”)

–Regarding educational innovation, the 'X+AI' plan stands out. Could you explain it in detail? (–교육 혁신과 관련해 ‘X+AI’ 구상이 눈에 띄는데, 구체적으로 설명하면.)

"X+AI is not a 'method of fitting majors around AI at the center,' but a structure where the major (X) is at the core and AI is used as the Wing. To this end, I proposed: △Making the 'Duksung Future Education Committee' a standing body directly under the president △Expanding the 'AI Convergence Education Support Center' within the Center for Teaching and Learning Development △Supporting AI professor-student practice (TAs and student tutors) △Expanding flexible academic systems (P/NP, blended learning, code sharing, etc.). Additionally, on the research and industry-academia front, I will establish five 'X+AI Convergence Research Clusters' directly under the president (Digital Humanities, AI New Drugs and Biohealth, Social Data Governance, AI Art & Tech, and AI-ESG Climate and Environment) to connect education, research, and industry." (“X+AI는 “AI 중심에 전공을 끼워 맞추는 방식”이 아니라, 전공(X)을 Core에 두고 AI를 Wing으로 활용하는 구조다. 이를 위해 △총장 직속 ‘덕성 미래교육 위원회’ 상설화 △교수학습개발센터의 ‘AI 융합교육 지원센터’ 확대 △AI 교수–학생 실습 지원(TA·학생 튜터) △유연 학사제도(P/NP, 블렌디드 러닝, 코드쉐어링 등) 확대를 제시했다. 또한, 연구·산학 측면에서는 총장 직속 ‘5대 X+AI 융합 연구 클러스터’(디지털 인문학, AI 신약·바이오헬스, 소셜데이터 거버넌스, AI 아트&테크, AI-ESG 기후환경) 구축을 통해 교육-연구-산학이 연결되도록 하겠다.”)

–You said you would make 'Bright Duksung, Together We Challenge' the university's operating principle during your term. Can you elaborate? (–임기 동안 ‘Bright 덕성, 함께하는 도전’을 대학의 운영 원칙으로 삼겠다고 했는데.)

"'Bright Duksung' is not just a slogan but a university operating principle. Based on six pillars—Balance, Respect, Innovation, Global, Harmony, and Talent—it is a vision to achieve harmony in education, research, and administration, and to realize a human-centered prestigious Duksung. The detailed operating principles can be summarized as: △B(Balance): Balance between financial soundness and future investment △R(Respect): A campus where respect for students, faculty, and staff is embodied in systems △I(Innovation): AI and data-based educational and administrative innovation △G(Global): Expanding international educational infrastructure and making global experiences a part of everyday life △H(Harmony): An educational philosophy where AI and HI (Human Intelligence) coexist △T(Talent): Customized talent development and integrated support for career, employment, and entrepreneurship." (“‘Bright 덕성’은 단순한 슬로건이 아니라 대학 운영 원칙이다. 균형(Balance), 존중(Respect), 혁신(Innovation), 글로벌(Global), 조화(Harmony), 인재(Talent)라는 여섯 축을 바탕으로, 교육·연구·행정의 조화를 이루고, 사람 중심의 명문 덕성을 구현하겠다는 비전이다. 세부적인 운영 원칙은 △B(Balance): 재정 건전성과 미래 투자의 균형 △R(Respect): 학생·교수·직원의 존중이 제도로 구현되는 캠퍼스 △I(Innovation): AI·데이터 기반 교육·행정 혁신 △G(Global): 국제 교육 인프라 확충과 글로벌 경험의 일상화 △H(Harmony): AI와 HI(인간지능)가 공존하는 교육 철학 △T(Talent): 맞춤형 인재육성, 진로·취업·창업의 통합 지원으로 요약할 수 있겠다.”)

–Lastly, is there anything you would like to say? (–끝으로 하고 싶은 말이 있다면.)

"In the AI era, universities cannot survive on rapid change alone. Ultimately, they must answer the question, 'What kind of people will we nurture, and how?' That is why Duksung must become a place that respects the diversity of majors while creating a 'human-centered advanced talent development model' where each major uses AI as a tool to grow on its own. During my four-year term, I will responsibly drive the process of that change so that it earns the trust of our members, is felt by students, and leads to tangible results for society." (“AI 시대에 대학은 빠른 변화만으로는 살아남기 어렵다. 결국은 ‘어떤 사람을 어떻게 길러낼 것인가’에 대한 답을 해야 한다. 그래서 덕성은 전공의 다양성을 존중하면서도, 각 전공이 AI를 도구로 삼아 스스로 성장할 수 있는 ‘사람 중심 첨단 인재양성 모델’을 만드는 곳이 되어야 한다. 4년간의 임기 동안 추진하고자 하는 그 변화의 과정이 구성원에게 신뢰받고, 학생에게 체감되며, 사회에 성과로 이어지도록 책임감 있게 추진하도록 하겠다.”)

Reporter Kim Mi-young kimmy@hani.co.kr, Photo provided by Duksung Women's University (김미영 기자 kimmy@hani.co.kr, 사진 덕성여대 제공)

New Departments Established: Virtual Reality Convergence, Data Science, and AI New Drugs (가상현실융합학과·데이터사이언스학과·AI신약학과 신설)

Full Liberal Arts Admission System Implemented…One Year for Academic and Career Exploration (전면 자유전공제 시행…1년간 학문과 진로 탐색)

( )

( )

Under the liberal arts admission system, Duksung Women's University students do not declare a major upon admission. Instead, they enter under a broad division and spend their first year exploring various fields through major exploration courses and liberal arts courses, gaining time for broad academic and career exploration. When they advance to their second year, they choose their majors. They may select their first major within their affiliated college and their second major from any college without restriction. Through this, students can establish their identity and design their own futures according to their aptitudes and abilities. Starting with the 2025 academic year, a new Division of Liberal Arts Studies has been established to provide even broader support for students' autonomous career design. (자유전공제에 따라 덕성여대 학생들은 입학 시 전공을 정하지 않고, 계열로 입학해 1년간 전공탐색과목과 교양과목을 통해 다양한 분야를 경험하며 폭넓은 학문과 진로 탐색의 시간을 갖는다. 2학년 진학 시 전공을 선택하게 되는데, 제1전공을 자신의 소속대학에서, 제2전공을 소속대학 구분 없이 선택할 수 있다. 이를 통해 학생들은 자신의 정체성을 바로 세우고, 자신의 적성과 능력에 따라 미래를 직접 설계할 수 있다. 2025학년도부터는 자유전공학부를 신설해 학생의 자율적 진로 설계를 더욱 폭 넓게 지원하고 있다.)

In addition, keeping pace with the AI era, the College of Future Talent has successively established advanced departments such as the Department of Virtual Reality Convergence, the Department of Data Science, the Department of AI New Drugs, and the Climate Environment and Culture major, building an academic structure that responds to future industrial demand. As a result, the university earned the highest grade, S, in the performance evaluation of the University Innovation Support Project for two consecutive years (2024 and 2025). The goal is to cultivate the Korean Studies major and Korean Language Education Program within the College of Future Talent as a cradle for nurturing K-content professionals. (여기에 더해 AI 시대에 발맞춰 미래인재대학에 가상현실융합학과, 데이터사이언스학과, AI신약학과, 기후환경과문화전공 등 첨단 분야 학과를 잇달아 신설하며 미래 산업 수요에 대응하는 학사구조를 갖춰가고 있다. 그 결과 2024년도 및 2025학년도 2년 연속 대학혁신지원사업 성과평가 최우수 등급인 S등급을 획득했다. 미래인재대학 내 한국학전공과 한국어교육과정은 K-콘텐츠 전문인력 양성의 요람으로 육성하는 것이 목표다.)

Since President Min Jae-hong took office, Duksung Women's University's innovation has shone even brighter. Plans are underway to progressively implement the strengthening of basic AI competency education, expansion of interdisciplinary majors, activation of self-designed majors and Nano/Microdegree programs (advanced courses of 6-15 credits), and the expansion of code sharing (mutual recognition of certain courses through agreements between departments). (민재홍 총장 취임 후 덕성여대의 혁신은 한층 더 빛을 발하고 있다. AI 기초역량 교육 강화, 융합전공 확대, 자기설계전공과 나노(Nano)·마이크로디그리(Microdegree·6~15학점 규모의 심화 교육과정) 활성화, 코드셰어링(Code Sharing·학과 간 협약으로 특정 과목을 공동으로 인정) 확대 등을 점진적으로 추진할 계획이다.)

To ensure that all students can build AI utilization capabilities on the foundation of their majors, the development of 'AI Bridge' courses, 'Duksung AI Literacy' classes, and a support system for AI-converged instruction within each major are also being established. Through these efforts, students will cultivate the ability to define and solve problems on their own, continuing the tradition of nurturing creative, convergent AI talent. Separately, the transition from the 'course retake system' to a 'grade forfeiture system' is also scheduled for implementation. (모든 학생이 전공 기반 위에서 AI 활용 역량을 갖출 수 있도록 ‘AI 브릿지’ 과목 개발 및 ‘덕성 AI 리터러시’ 수업, 전공별 AI 융합 수업 지원 체계도 구축되는데, 이를 통해 학생 스스로 문제를 정의하고 해결하는 힘까지 기르게 함으로써, 창의적 융·복합 AI 인재 양성의 전통을 이어가겠다는 것이다. 이와 별개로 ‘재수강 제도’의 ‘학점포기제’로 전환도 시행을 앞두고 있다.)

Reporter Kim Mi-young (김미영 기자)

item.title: What Do Our Children's Gaming Habits Reveal About Them? (게임으로 알 수 있는 우리 아이들의 성향은?)
item.description:
Joo Hanna | Former Microsoft Researcher & Data Scientist
 
 In our home, every day brings something reminiscent—if not quite equal to—a high-stakes negotiation table among world leaders, but it's a fierce "negotiation war" nonetheless, and it's all about gaming time. ( 주한나 | 전 미국 마이크로소프트 연구원·데이터 과학자
 
 우리집에서는 세계 정상들의 국제관계 협상 테이블을 방불케하게까지는 않더라도 어쨌든 치열한 ‘네고전쟁’(negotiation war)이 매일같이 일어나는데 그것은 게임시간 관련이다.)

With youth smartphone and gaming addiction emerging as a serious social issue, I'm surely not the only parent waging war over whether to allow gaming and for how long. (청소년의 스마트폰과 게임 중독의 문제가 심각한 사회 문제로 떠오른 만큼, 자녀의 게임 허용 여부와 시간을 놓고 전쟁을 벌이는 부모는 나뿐만이 아닐 것이다.)

Kids genuinely love gaming. They likely spend far more time gaming than they do with school friends. No matter how much I lecture from the sidelines that "games only inject a manufactured, fake sense of achievement, much like junk food with zero nutritional value, making it harder to find real fulfillment in life," it has little effect. (아이들은 게임을 정말 좋아한다. 학교 친구와 보내는 시간보다 게임으로 보내는 시간이 훨씬 더 많을 것이다. 그 옆에서 내가 “게임은 인공적으로 만들어낸 가짜 성취감을 주입할 뿐이며, 이것은 곧 영양가 없는 정크 푸드와 같아서 실생활에서 성취감을 얻기 더 힘들게 한다”고 아무리 설교해봐야 별 효과는 없다.)

Instead, kids argue they experience achievement, challenge, cooperation, and world-building through games. If I can't understand what my child loves, it won't do any favors for our relationship. (오히려 아이는 게임에서 성취감, 도전, 협동, 세계 구축의 경험을 한다고 주장한다. 아이가 좋아하는 것을 내가 전혀 이해하지 못하면 관계 개선에 도움이 될 리가 없다.)

When a child makes a new friend, parents are deeply curious about what kind of kid that friend is. The same goes for gaming. It's only natural for parents to wonder what games their children are playing. I've heard so much advice about needing to know my children's games well that I've tried it myself a few times. What I've keenly felt is that there are far too many types to lump together under "games," and my children's tastes are so different from mine that I'd suspect a genetic anomaly. (아이가 새 친구를 사귀게 되면 부모는 그 아이가 어떤 아이인지 아주 궁금해한다. 게임도 마찬가지다. 부모가 자녀가 무슨 게임을 하는지 궁금해하는 것은 당연하다. 자녀가 하는 게임을 잘 알아야 한다는 조언을 하도 들어서 나도 몇 번 도전해보았다. 절절하게 느낀 것은 ‘게임’으로 뭉뚱그리기에는 너무나도 많은 종류가 있고, 아이들의 취향은 유전자가 의심될 정도로 나와 다르다는 것이다.)

So I asked artificial intelligence (AI) to broadly categorize game types. A child who enjoys FPS or battle royale games like Fortnite or Overwatch is drawn to immediate feedback and clear win-loss outcomes. They excel at quick focus and love making fast decisions under pressure. (그리하여 인공지능(AI)에게 게임 종류를 크게 나눠 달라고 부탁해보았다. 포트나이트, 오버워치 같은 FPS·배틀로얄을 즐기는 아이는 즉각적인 피드백과 명확한 승패에 끌린다. 순간 집중력이 뛰어나고 압박 상황에서 빠르게 판단하는 걸 좋아한다.)

A child who likes creative or sandbox games like Minecraft or The Sims enjoys the process more than the result. They thrive on building things bit by bit and living off the pride of "I made this." (마인크래프트, 심즈 같은 창작·샌드박스 게임을 좋아하는 아이는 결과보다 과정을 즐긴다. 조금씩 쌓아가며 “내가 만들었다”는 자부심을 먹고 자란다.)

A child who enjoys social or party games like Among Us, Animal Crossing, or Mario Kart is relationship-oriented. Who they play with matters more than winning. Team sports or club activities suit them well, and careers like teaching, event planning, or HR would align with their strengths. (어몽어스, 동물의 숲, 마리오카트 같은 소셜·파티 게임을 즐기는 아이는 관계 중심적이다. 이기는 것보다 누구와 하는지가 더 중요하다. 팀 스포츠나 동아리 활동이 맞고, 교사·이벤트 기획자·HR 전문가가 적성과 잘 어울리는 직업이다.)

Of course, not every game fits neatly into these categories. Roblox alone is a platform containing millions of different experiences. Saying "I play Roblox" doesn't tell you much about a child. What matters is what they do inside it—and sitting down beside them to look together is the most honest approach. A child's heart opens just from knowing their parent takes an interest in their world. (물론 모든 게임이 이런 식으로 각각 분류에 맞아 떨어지지 않는다. 로블록스만 해도 수백만 개의 서로 다른 체험이 담긴 플랫폼이다. “로블록스 한다”는 말만으로는 아이를 알 수 없다. 그 안에서 무엇을 하는지, 옆에 앉아서 함께 들여다보는 것이 가장 정직한 방법이다. 아이는 부모가 자기 세계에 관심을 가져준다는 것만으로도 마음을 연다.)

Once you have a rough grasp, using AI can be helpful too. Input something like, "My child loves ○○ game; analyze its characteristics and recommend activities and aptitudes they might enjoy," and you'll get fairly specific answers. Parents don't need to be gaming experts. You can also simply ask your child directly: "What do you like most about the game?" Is it winning, creating, the story, or playing with friends? That single answer can reveal more than you'd expect. (어느 정도 파악이 됐다면, AI를 활용하는 것도 좋다. “우리 아이가 ○○ 게임을 좋아하는데, 이 게임의 특성을 분석해서 아이가 좋아할 만한 활동과 적성을 추천해줘”라고 입력하면 꽤 구체적인 답이 돌아온다. 부모가 게임 전문가가 아니어도 된다. 아이에게 직접 물어봐도 된다. “게임에서 뭐가 제일 좋아?” 이기는 것인지, 만드는 것인지, 이야기인지, 친구랑 같이 하는 것인지. 그 대답 하나가 의외로 많은 걸 알려준다.)

Gaming doesn't have to be a waste of time. It can be a window into what draws your child in and how they experience the world. Before unplugging the console, let's take a look inside the screen first. (게임은 시간 낭비가 아닐 수 있다. 아이가 무엇에 끌리고, 어떤 방식으로 세계를 경험하는지를 보여주는 창일 수 있다. 전원을 뽑기 전에, 먼저 화면 속을 들여다보자.)

item.title: “No stage? No problem—just add a spoonful of imagination” (“무대 없어도 괜찮아요, 상상력 한 스푼만 더하면”)
item.description:
The tvN variety show “After School, Teacher Tae-ri” is making waves. It’s a program where actress Kim Tae-ri opens an after-school theater class at a small rural elementary school and builds a stage production with children who have never done theater before. As they try their hand at acting for the very first time, the kids gradually discover their own ways of expressing themselves. You don’t need a stage or an audience for it to count. Just adding a spoonful of imagination to everyday life is enough to set the theater in motion. Tonight, pull out a picture book and say to your child, “Shall we act out this scene?” (tvN 예능 ‘방과후 태리쌤’이 화제다. 배우 김태리가 작은 시골 초등학교에 방과후 연극반을 열고, 연극이 처음인 아이들과 무대를 만들어가는 프로그램이다. 난생처음 연극에 도전하면서 아이들은 조금씩 자신만의 표현을 찾아간다. 꼭 무대와 관객이 갖춰지지 않아도 괜찮다. 일상에 상상력 한 스푼을 더하는 것만으로도 연극은 시작된다. 오늘 저녁, 그림책 한 권을 꺼내 아이에게 말해보자. “우리 이 장면 한번 연기해볼까?”)

Theater activities that safely open up the world of imagination (안전하게 상상의 세계를 열어주는 연극 활동)

When people hear the word “theater,” they often picture a grand stage, dazzling lights, and actors performing with all their might beneath them. That’s why theater activities feel appealing yet hard to jump into. But children, in fact, naturally experience theatrical play from a young age through make-believe. Playing doctor, playing school, playing store—these everyday role-playing games are the starting point of theater. All you need is the mindset of expanding that role-playing into something a little more structured and varied. (연극이라고 하면 화려한 무대와 조명, 그 아래에서 열연을 펼치는 배우들의 모습이 먼저 떠오른다. 그래서 연극 활동은 매력적이지만 쉽게 도전하기 어려운 영역으로 여겨지기도 한다. 그러나 아이들은 사실 어릴 때부터 놀이를 통해 자연스럽게 연극적 활동을 경험한다. 병원놀이, 학교놀이, 마트놀이 등 일상에서 즐기는 역할 놀이가 바로 연극의 출발점이다. 이러한 역할 놀이를 좀더 체계적이고 다양하게 확장해본다는 마음이면 충분하다.)

Theater is a medium that lets children safely encounter a wide range of worlds on a fictional stage. Kids can freely experience situations in stories that would be hard to face in real life, and by becoming characters different from themselves—animals, or even objects—they can build empathy and a sense of self. It’s also highly effective for nurturing self-expression and initiative. (연극은 다양한 세상을 허구의 무대에서 안전하게 만나게 해주는 매개다. 아이들은 현실에서는 겪기 어려운 상황을 이야기 속에서 마음껏 경험하고, 나와 다른 인물이나 동물, 심지어 사물이 되어보는 과정을 통해 공감 능력과 자아를 키울 수 있다. 자기 표현력과 능동성을 키우는 데도 효과적이다.)

Lee Ji-hyun, a theater arts instructor and author of “Picture Book Theater Class” (School Library Journal Press), speaks to the benefits: “A child with a tiny voice, a child who never raised their hand, a child too afraid of giving the wrong answer—through theater class activities, they find themselves raising their hand and speaking up without even realizing it.” This applies not just to young children but to teenagers as well. During the period when self-identity takes shape, the experience of playing various roles helps them see themselves objectively and understand others’ perspectives. (‘그림책 연극 수업’((주)학교도서관저널)의 저자인 이지현 연극예술 강사는 “목소리가 작았던 아이, 발표를 못했던 아이, 정답이 아닐까 봐 무서워했던 아이가 연극 수업 활동을 하면서 자신도 모르게 손을 들고, 크게 말하게 된다”라면서 연극 활동의 효과를 이야기한다. 이는 유아·어린이뿐 아니라 청소년에게도 마찬가지다. 자아 정체성이 형성되는 시기에 다양한 인물을 연기해보는 경험은 자신을 객관화하고 타인의 관점을 이해하는 데 도움이 된다.)

Theatrical activities to try in everyday life (일상에서 시도해보는 연극적 활동)

–Seeing is believing: go watch a play first (–백문이 불여일견, 먼저 연극 보러 가기)

Before diving into theater activities, take your child to see a live performance. Pick a show that suits their age and interests, and as you watch together, the vivid energy of the stage and actors can naturally spark a “I want to try that too” feeling. It’s also a great chance to learn theater etiquette—the unspoken rules of being an audience member—together. (연극 활동을 본격적으로 시작하기 전, 아이와 공연을 직접 보러 가보자. 아이의 연령대와 관심사에 맞는 공연을 골라 함께 관람하다 보면, 무대와 배우의 생생한 에너지를 통해 ‘나도 해보고 싶다’는 마음이 자연스럽게 생겨날 수 있다. 공연장에서 지켜야 할 약속, 즉 연극 에티켓을 함께 익히는 것도 좋은 경험이다.)

–Express with faces and bodies instead of words (–말 대신 표정과 몸짓으로 표현해보기)

If you’re new to theater activities, start with a warm-up. Try a game where the caregiver and child look at cards with different emotion words and act them out with facial expressions for the other to guess. From “joyful face” to “terrified face” to “wronged face,” you can act out a range of emotions in silence while learning about different feelings and how to show them. (연극 활동이 처음이라면 워밍업부터 시작해보자. 보호자와 아이가 다양한 감정 단어 카드를 보면서 표정으로 표현하고 맞춰보는 게임을 추천한다. ‘기쁜 얼굴’ ‘겁에 질린 얼굴’ ‘억울한 얼굴’ 등 다양한 감정을 말없이 연기하면서 여러 감정과 표현 방법을 익혀나갈 수 있다.)

From there, you could try pantomime, one of theater’s key techniques—expressing a specific situation or emotion purely through body movement, no words. You might act out a scene from a picture book or a play, or even a moment from daily life. (나아가 연극적 표현 방법 중 하나인 팬터마임을 시도해봐도 좋다. 대사 없이 몸짓만으로 특정 상황이나 감정을 표현하는 방식이다. 그림책이나 희곡 속 한 장면을 팬터마임으로 표현해볼 수도 있고, 일상 속 한 장면을 표현해봐도 된다.)

Lee Ji-hyun suggests: “How about trying to show, without speaking, everything from waking up this morning to stepping out of the school entrance—using only your face and body?” She notes that everyday actions can be turned into movement exercises, and as you go, you can point out what’s missing or under-expressed, refining your expressive skills along the way. (이지현 강사는 “오늘 아침에 일어나서 학교 현관을 나설 때까지 모습을 말하지 말고 표정과 행동으로만 표현해볼까?”라고 하면서 일상에서 자주 하는 행동을 몸짓으로 표현해볼 수 있다고 조언한다. 그 과정에서 생략되거나 표현이 부족한 부분들을 함께 짚으면서 표현력을 풍부하게 다듬을 수 있다.)

–Improv theater games with picture books (–그림책을 활용한 즉흥극 놀이)

Picture books are a wonderful tool for theater activities. Lee Ji-hyun cites their accessibility as the biggest strength: “Picture books have little text and pair images with words, making them easy to approach. And the more you read them, the more you can uncover something of your own in them.” (그림책은 연극 활동에 활용할 수 있는 좋은 도구다. 이지현 강사는 그림책의 가장 큰 장점으로 만만함을 꼽는다. “그림책은 글밥이 적고 그림과 글이 함께 있어 접근이 쉬운 도구다. 동시에 읽을 수록 자신만의 무언가를 발굴해낼 수 있다는 매력도 있다.”)

Lee’s “Picture Book Theater Class” introduces a variety of theater activities built around picture books. You can choose a book based on your child’s age and interests and experiment with different theatrical expressions. For example, “I Shouldn’t Have Taken It Off” is a picture book that playfully imagines a child wriggling around after getting stuck while taking off clothes. After reading it, you can imagine a similar situation and act it out as an improvisation. (이지현 강사의 ‘그림책 연극 수업’에는 그림책을 매개로 한 다양한 연극 활동이 소개되어 있다. 아이의 연령과 관심사에 따라 그림책을 선택하고 여러 연극적 표현을 시도해볼 수 있다. 일례로 ‘벗지 말걸 그랬어’는 옷을 벗다가 걸려서 버둥거리는 아이의 이야기를 재미있는 상상력으로 담아낸 그림책이다. 이 책을 읽고 그림책과 같은 상황을 상상하고 즉흥극으로 표현해볼 수 있다.)

When starting theater work with picture books, begin by simply following the scenes or dialogue as written. Once you’re comfortable, you can expand endlessly—by changing the ending or introducing new characters. (그림책으로 연극 활동을 할 때 처음에는 책의 장면이나 대사를 그대로 따라하는 것으로 시작, 익숙해지면 결말을 바꾸거나 새로운 캐릭터를 등장시키는 방식으로 얼마든지 확장할 수 있다.)

–Today I’m the mom: role-swapping activities (–오늘은 내가 엄마, 역할 바꾸기 활동)

Try swapping roles. A caregiver and child can trade places, or close friends can act as each other. When a caregiver and child do role-play in particular, the child gets a taste of the parent’s perspective while the parent gains a chance to think from the child’s point of view. One caution: if you use it as a teaching moment, only acting out the things the child usually gets wrong, it can breed resentment toward the activity. Instead, make it a chance to observe each other closely and capture each other’s quirks—turning it into a way to reaffirm your affection for one another. With a teenager, this can even surface subtle conflicts that are hard to put into words in everyday conversation, opening a channel for communication you didn’t expect. (서로의 역할을 바꾸어 연기해보자. 보호자와 아이가 역할을 바꿀 수도 있고, 친한 친구끼리 서로를 연기해볼 수도 있다. 특히 보호자와 아이가 역할극을 하면 아이는 부모의 입장을 간접적으로 경험하고, 부모 역시 아이의 입장에서 생각해보는 계기를 만들 수 있다. 이때 아이에게 교훈을 주려는 목적으로 평소 아이가 잘 못하는 부분만 연기하면 활동에 대한 반감이 오히려 커질 수 있다. 상대방을 잘 관찰하고 특징을 표현함으로써, 오히려 서로에 대한 애정을 확인하는 계기로 삼아보자. 청소년 자녀와 함께하면 평소 대화로는 하기 어려웠던 미묘한 갈등을 드러내고 소통의 물꼬를 트는 뜻밖의 효과를 볼 수도 있다.)

Want to go further? Put on a show (조금 더 나아가고 싶다면, 공연 올리기)

If you want to take it a step beyond, try staging an actual performance. Rehearsing a complete play and bringing it to a stage gives children an unforgettable experience. It doesn’t have to be grand. Start with a short performance just for the family. You could gather neighborhood kids to prepare a play together, or set up a class production in the classroom. (한 단계 더 나아가 직접 무대 공연까지 시도해봐도 좋다. 한편의 완결된 연극을 연습하고 무대에 올리는 일은 아이들에게 잊을 수 없는 경험을 선사한다. 거창하지 않아도 괜찮다. 가족끼리 짧은 공연을 올리는 것부터 시작해보자. 동네 아이들을 모아 함께 연극을 준비하거나, 교실에서 학급 연극 무대를 꾸며봐도 좋다.)

When preparing a performance, first pick a script or story. A picture book works well, or you can find suitable scripts online. Older kids might adapt a novel or film themselves. Once the script is chosen, take time to explore the plot, the characters’ traits, and their emotions together. After casting, read the script aloud in character and map out the blocking—where everyone stands and how they move. For costumes and props, using what’s already at home is more than enough. Mom’s scarf becomes a king’s cape; an umbrella transforms into a magic wand. The very process of imagining what each object could become and dressing the stage is a rich creative exercise. And the moment after the show when everyone applauds each other—that’s when a child feels, in every fiber, the pride of having made something together. (공연을 준비할 때는 대본이나 이야기를 먼저 고른다. 그림책을 활용해도 좋고, 인터넷에서 적절한 대본을 찾는 방법도 있다. 청소년이라면 원작 소설이나 영화를 직접 각색해볼 수도 있다. 대본이 정해지면 줄거리와 인물의 성격, 감정을 함께 탐색하는 시간을 갖자. 배역이 정해지면 각자 맡은 인물로 대본을 소리 내어 읽어보고, 어느 위치에서 어떻게 움직일지 동선을 함께 정한다. 의상이나 소품은 집에 있는 것들을 활용하면 충분하다. 엄마의 스카프가 왕의 망토가 되고, 우산이 마법 지팡이로 변신한다. 어떤 물건이 무엇으로 변할 수 있을지 상상하며 무대를 꾸미는 과정 자체가 훌륭한 창작 활동이다. 공연이 끝난 후 서로에게 박수를 보내는 그 순간, 아이는 함께 무언가를 만들어냈다는 성취감을 온몸으로 느끼게 된다.)

Structured theater programs to discover (프로그램으로 만나는 체계적인 연극 활동)

It’s also worth looking into programs led by professional instructors. They offer a more systematic, polished way to experience and learn theater. Local cultural foundations, libraries, and children’s theater companies offer a wide range of programs for kids. (전문 강사가 이끄는 프로그램을 찾아보는 것도 추천한다. 더 체계적이고 전문적인 방법으로 연극을 접하고 배울 수 있다. 각 지역의 문화재단, 도서관, 어린이 극단 등에서 아이들을 대상으로 한 관련 프로그램을 다양하게 찾아볼 수 있다.)

Seo Suwon Library will hold an interactive 3D reading performance called “Book Play Theater” on April 12. Featuring a polar bear character and tales like “The Farting Daughter-in-Law” and “Grandma Patjuk and the Tiger,” the program lets children follow along with songs and movements. It’s aimed at ages 5 through second grade. Registration is available on the Seo Suwon Library website and the Suwon City Library app. (서수원도서관은 오는 4월12일 체험형 입체낭독극 ‘책놀이 연극’을 진행한다. 북극곰 캐릭터와 함께 ‘방귀쟁이 며느리’ ‘팥죽할머니와 호랑이’ 이야기를 만나며 노래와 율동을 직접 따라 해볼 수 있는 프로그램으로, 만 5살부터 초등학교 2학년을 대상으로 한다. 참가 신청은 서수원도서관 누리집과 수원시도서관 앱에서 할 수 있다.)

In Gwangju, the Asia Culture Center Foundation is recruiting members for “Dream Theater Gwangju Dong-gu,” a program for local children and youth. Running every Thursday from April 23 to November 22, it’s a creative program where participants experience the entire process of putting on a performance firsthand. Tuition is fully free, and details can be found on the foundation’s website (www.accf.or.kr). (광주에서는 국립아시아문화전당재단이 지역 아동·청소년을 위한 ‘꿈의 극단 광주 동구’ 단원을 모집한다. 오는 4월23일부터 11월22일까지 매주 목요일 진행하는 해당 프로그램은 공연이 만들어지는 전 과정을 직접 체험하는 창작 활동이다. 교육비는 전액 무료이며, 자세한 내용은 재단 누리집(www.accf.or.kr)에서 확인하면 된다.)

Dream Theater Gwanak is a culture and arts education program for teenagers. In 2026, it’s recruiting the second cohort of “We Are Heroes,” which guides participants through expression training in acting, voice, and choreography, along with a creative process, to complete a full musical performance. The program runs from April to November, with applications open until April 7. For more information and inquiries, contact the Gwanak Cultural Foundation (gfac.or.kr). (꿈의 극단 관악은 청소년을 대상으로 하는 문화예술교육 프로그램이다. 2026년에는 연기, 발성, 안무 등의 표현 교육과 창작 과정을 통해 하나의 뮤지컬 공연을 완성하는 ‘우리가 영웅’ 2기 단원을 모집한다. 활동기간은 4월부터 11월까지이며, 4월 7일까지 참여자를 모집한다. 자세한 사항 확인 및 문의는 관악문화재단(gfac.or.kr)에서 가능하다.)

Park Eun-ah, contributing correspondent (박은아 객원기자)
